sources.title: D. Aharonov and M. Ben-Or, Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Constant Error, arXiv:quant-ph/9611025v2 (1996)
sources.locator: Complete 18-page PDF read sequentially. Inspected §2.2, §§3.1–3.3, §4.1, §§5.1–5.2, and Appendices A–E (PDF pp.1–18); the threshold derivation is in §4.1 and Appendix C (PDF pp.8–15).

contents.name: §2.2, finite independent local-fault model and fault paths
contents.reason: The item formalizes independent fault indicators, declared finite locations, local CPTP replacement maps, and a separate correlated-noise branch.

contents.name: §3.1, Definition 1, sparse and deviated states
contents.reason: The source motivates support-limited errors, while the local definition uses the audited Kraus-span condition and retains an arbitrary reference rather than relying only on reduced-state equality.

contents.name: §3.2, Definition 2, computation-code gates and spread
contents.reason: The local gadget contract makes input and output registers, ideal actions, locations, spread, correction capacity, branches, and recursive gate-set closure explicit.

contents.name: §3.3, Lemma 1, one-level sparse-path deviation
contents.reason: The batch supplies an explicit reference-preserving support-count proof under the stated one-level computation and correction contracts.

contents.name: §3.3, Theorem 1, one-level effective fault probability
contents.reason: The local proof derives the exact q+1-child union bound and distinguishes the child-count parameter from the elementary-location count.

contents.name: §4.1, Definitions 4–6, proper codes and recursive sparse rectangles
contents.reason: The definitions are retained with explicit level-zero cases, disjoint child-location sets, and a separate correctness contract for good gadgets.

contents.name: §4.1, Lemma 2 and Theorem 2; Appendix C, concatenated recurrence and overhead
contents.reason: The item proves the conditional recurrence, the output trace-distance and measurement-law bounds, and the least-level polylogarithmic overhead consequence.

contents.name: §2.2, independent local-fault model; not a correlated subset-bound result
contents.reason: The paper models independent per-location faults in §2.2. Its full text does not state the correlated local-stochastic subset law; the batch uses AGP08 for that definition and proves the witness recurrence locally.

contents.name: §5.1, Theorem 3 and Appendix D, linear-code qubit gadget blueprint
contents.reason: The explicit code claim remains in the inventory, but this source's gadget construction is only a blueprint for the complete local universal-family proof.

contents.name: §5.2, Theorem 4 and Appendix E, polynomial qupit code family
contents.reason: The current explicit-instantiation obligation follows the finite-qubit Steane and distance-three branches; a separate polynomial qupit family and its gate proofs are not needed for that claim.

contents.name: Appendix A, Lemma 3, majority readout from a deviated encoded block
contents.reason: The local contract requires a fully specified readout gadget and reference-preserving output branch; the source's majority procedure is not used as a substitute for that contract.

contents.name: Appendix B, Lemma 4, metric properties of reduced-state deviation
contents.reason: The local page does not use this reduced-state metric; it defines deviation by a supported Kraus-span channel with the reference system retained.

contents.name: §6, nearest-neighbor gate extension
contents.reason: The assigned page claims no nearest-neighbor architecture or locality overhead, so that separate geometric circuit construction is not part of its theorem.

contents.name: §2.2, chronological fault locations and finite fault paths
contents.reason: The paper defines time-resolved locations and fault paths; this item makes the recursive rectangle partitions, overlap convention, and separate a/b counts explicit.

contents.name: §2.2, product law for independent location faults
contents.reason: The paper supplies the independent-location special case; the local proof expands events into finitely many indicator patterns and sums the product law.

contents.name: §2.2, independent fault paths as a special case
contents.reason: The independent Bernoulli model satisfies the subset bound, but does not supply the general correlated local-stochastic definition.

contents.name: §4.1 and Appendix C, recursive sparse-rectangle route
contents.reason: The source motivates recursive witness counting. The local lemma proves its finite witness recurrence directly from the subset-bound definition and disjoint child-location sets.

contents.name: §3.3 and §4.1, fault and rectangle terminology
contents.reason: The local definition specifies the finite location hierarchy, elementary location sets, and distinct ordinary and extended rectangle conventions.

contents.name: §4.1, distance-one extended-rectangle remark
contents.reason: The source notes a separate distance-one branch. This item proves only the recurrence conditional on an explicit disjoint-witness reduction; the truncation and overlap proof remains unresolved.

contents.name: §2.2, finite mixture of conditional circuit denotations
contents.reason: The source identifies the weighted mixture over independent fault paths; this item supplies the local finite CPTP-mixture proof.

contents.name: §2.2, finite ordered faulty-location circuits
contents.reason: The paper fixes finite time-ordered locations with arbitrary local operations at faulty slots; QC21 states the finite full-register channel schedule explicitly and proves its denotation is CPTP from channel composition.

sources.title: John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 7: Quantum Error Correction
sources.locator: Inspected §7.18.3–7.18.6, printed pp.55–59 (PDF pp.61–65), including equations (7.239)–(7.242), the iid-Z path count, minimum-weight recovery, and the explicit perfect-syndrome limitation.

contents.name: §7.18.3–7.18.4, CSS recovery, planar geometry, and minimum-weight decoding
contents.reason: The current QC20 supplier body states the nontrivial-logical-path interface; the new local lemma proves the minimum-weight comparison that forces at least half the path edges to be actual errors. Supplier transitive prerequisites remain to be reconciled.

contents.name: §7.18.5, equations (7.239)–(7.242), path probability and threshold sum
contents.reason: The local proof reproduces the finite union bound and geometric-series estimate with the task's explicit d+1 boundary-count convention.

contents.name: §7.18.6, circuit-level syndrome and gate-error qualification
contents.reason: The item is explicitly an ideal-syndrome memory theorem and does not claim that the iid data-error estimate proves a faulty-gate circuit threshold.

contents.name: §7.18.3–7.18.4, minimum-weight planar recovery path argument
contents.reason: The local proof matches perfect syndromes to relative cycles, uses the current QC20 nontrivial-support path statement, and proves by a same-syndrome path toggle that at least half the crossing-path edges are actual errors.

contents.name: Finite distance-five geometric-series instance
contents.reason: The example evaluates the local theorem at d=5 and ε=1/144; its arithmetic is finite and the perfect-syndrome limitation is stated explicitly.

contents.name: §7.18.6, circuit-level syndrome and gate-error qualification
contents.reason: The chapter distinguishes circuit-level gate and syndrome operations from the ideal-syndrome memory estimate; QC21 models each supplied operation as a local channel in an explicit finite schedule.

sources.title: John Preskill, Toric code recovery, fault-tolerant recovery, fault-tolerant gates (2011 handwritten lecture notes)

Relevant text: pp.1–3 toric-memory path estimate, pp.4–8 t=1 memory-recovery properties and ancillas, pp.16–25 transversal Clifford and magic-state T-gadget material. The source ledger reports full visual inspection; this author does not rely on its nonextractable circuit diagrams.

contents.name: pp.1–3, toric-code memory recovery and iid-Z path estimate
contents.reason: The text corroborates the narrow memory setting, but the theorem's exact planar boundary count comes from the separate QC20 path interface.

contents.name: pp.4–8, t=1 recovery properties, repeated syndrome, and ancilla verification
contents.reason: The note supplies memory gadgets and local t=1 conditions, but not the complete gate, idle, preparation, readout, and overlap proof required by this item.

contents.name: pp.9–10, Pauli propagation and spread
contents.reason: The propagation discussion informs the declared spread interface; local readiness still depends on the actual QC18/QC19 support and recovery bodies.

contents.name: pp.16–20, Steane transversal Clifford gadgets
contents.reason: The explicit Steane route remains in the theorem inventory, while its complete universal gadget verification is still an authoring obligation.

contents.name: pp.21–25, verified magic-state injection and the T gadget
contents.reason: The text sketches a universal-gate route but does not provide the full concatenated circuit-threshold proof required by the local theorem.

sources.title: P. Aliferis, D. Gottesman, J. Preskill, Accuracy Threshold for Postselected Quantum Computation, Quantum Information and Computation 8 (2008), 181–244
sources.locator: Introduction, local stochastic fault-path definition; §4.1, “The trouble with local stochastic noise,” including the arbitrary fault-path operation and correlation discussion.

contents.name: Introduction and §4.1, local stochastic fault-set law
contents.reason: The paper defines the model by bounding the sum of probabilities of all fault paths containing any specified r locations by ε^r, with arbitrary operations on faulty locations.

contents.name: Introduction and §4.1, correlated conditional fault operations
contents.reason: The paper bounds every specified fault-location subset and allows an arbitrary operation at each faulty location, with the operation chosen for that fault path. QC21 permits the locationwise map choice to depend on the whole fault pattern but does not infer a single arbitrary joint channel across distinct locations.

contents.name: §4.1, local stochastic threshold context
contents.reason: The paper distinguishes the local-stochastic error-correction setting from its own postselected threshold, which does not handle strongly correlated adversarial noise. The local concatenated witness-count and output bounds are proved in this batch, not taken from that postselected theorem.

contents.name: §4.1, subset-bound input to recursive witness counting
contents.reason: The paper supplies the precise subset-probability hypothesis. The witness-count recurrence and closed form are proved locally from that hypothesis; the source is not treated as supplying the proof.

contents.name: Introduction and §4.1, finite fault-path channel schedule
contents.reason: The source defines time-step locations and arbitrary operations at faulty locations. QC21 turns this into a typed finite ordered schedule of full-register CPTP maps and proves the composition interface locally.
